reference_use.conclusion: The pinned project and SimonGMT contain no Lipschitz push-forward of normal currents, no products with [[0,1]] and no homotopy formula, so the supplied Parts 1–8 are new obligations. Their smooth-approximation, product and homotopy inputs come from the three unaccepted uncle nodes, which are therefore passed as explicit hypotheses. Five accepted declarations are reused by name with byte-identical types: compatible forms (R3), the support facts (S)/(F3c), the mass bound (R1), the pull-back norm bound (F7), and the continuity criterion for (F5/F6). No accepted lemma already turns a bounded linear functional into a current with a mass bound, so this becomes the new child current_criterion. Every Mathlib lemma cited in the child proofs exists in the pinned snapshot (extDeriv_pullback, EventuallyEq.extDeriv_eq, TendstoUniformlyOn.congr_right, IsCompact.cthickening, mem_cthickening_of_dist_le, self_subset_thickening, Fin.cons_self_tail, cauchySeq_tendsto_of_complete, tendsto_nhds_unique). All statements elaborate in the exact comparator scope. The parent follows from the children by a checked 4-line assembly, and each new child has an independent Lean proof modulo its declared dependencies. The dph_lpf_* names are globally unused.

subproblem.title: Comparison lemma: two locally admissible smooth approximations of G give asymptotically equal values X(η_n), via the homotopy formula and the affine estimate (supplied Step 1)
subproblem.statement: The following notation is that of the frozen statement of the sibling smooth_homotopy, quoted here: Notation: for s ∈ ℝ and x ∈ ℝ^m, cons(s, x) := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons s (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ x)) ∈ ℝ^{m+1}; ι(v) := cons(0, v); e₀ := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 ∈ ℝ^{m+1}; for y ∈ ℝ^{m+1}, t(y) := EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ y 0 and tl(y) := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ y)); cyl(A) := {y : t(y) ∈ [0,1], tl(y) ∈ A}. D_q(ℝ^p) := GeometricCurrentOn univ q, D^q(ℝ^p) := TestFormOn univ q, M = mass, spt = support, ∂ = boundary. For X ∈ D_k(ℝ^m) and Z ∈ D_{k+1}(ℝ^{m+1}), ProdChar(X, Z) means: for every η ∈ D^{k+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) and every φ : ℝ → D^k(ℝ^m) with φ(s)(x)(v_1, …, v_k) = η(cons(s, x))(e₀, ι(v_1), …, ι(v_k)) for all s ∈ [0,1], x ∈ ℝ^m, v ∈ (ℝ^m)^k (Fin.cons e₀ (ι ∘ v)), one has Z(η) = ∫_0^1 X(φ(s)) ds (interval integral). For g : ℝ^p → ℝ^q, ω ∈ D^j(ℝ^q), η ∈ D^j(ℝ^p) and A ⊆ ℝ^p, 'η is compatible with (g, ω) near A' means: there is an open N ⊇ A with η(x) = ω(g(x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ g x) for all x ∈ N. Here dω is exteriorDerivative ω. (E0) For all m, m′ ∈ ℕ, X ∈ D_0(ℝ^m) with M(X) < ∞, Z ∈ D_{0+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) with ProdChar(X, Z), and C^∞ G : ℝ^{m+1} → ℝ^{m′} with G⁻¹(K) ∩ cyl(spt X) compact for every compact K: for every ω ∈ D^0(ℝ^{m′}), all η₀, η₁ ∈ D^0(ℝ^m) such that η_i is compatible with (x ↦ G(cons(i, x)), ω) near spt X (i = 0, 1), and every η′ ∈ D^{0+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) compatible with (G, dω) near cyl(spt X): X(η₁) − X(η₀) = Z(η′). (E1) For all m, m′, j ∈ ℕ, X ∈ D_{j+1}(ℝ^m) with M(X) < ∞, Z ∈ D_{j+1+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) with ProdChar(X, Z), Z′ ∈ D_{j+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) with ProdChar(∂X, Z′), and G as in (E0): for every ω ∈ D^{j+1}(ℝ^{m′}), all η₀, η₁ ∈ D^{j+1}(ℝ^m) with η_i compatible with (x ↦ G(cons(i, x)), ω) near spt X, every η′ ∈ D^{j+1+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) compatible with (G, dω) near cyl(spt X) and every θ′ ∈ D^{j+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) compatible with (G, ω) near cyl(spt X): X(η₁) − X(η₀) = Z(η′) + Z′(θ′). (Aff) For all m, m′, k ∈ ℕ there is c ≥ 0 such that for all X ∈ D_k(ℝ^m), Z ∈ D_{k+1}(ℝ^{m+1}), C^∞ maps F₀, F₁ : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′}, open O ⊆ ℝ^m and s, L, B ∈ ℝ with 0 ≤ s, 0 ≤ L, 0 ≤ B, M(X) ≤ ofReal B, ProdChar(X, Z), spt X ⊆ O, dist(F₁(x), F₀(x)) ≤ s, ‖fderiv ℝ F₀ x‖ ≤ L and ‖fderiv ℝ F₁ x‖ ≤ L for x ∈ O, and F₀⁻¹(K) ∩ spt X compact for every compact K: for every ψ ∈ D^{k+1}(ℝ^{m′}), every C ∈ ℝ with covectorEuclideanNorm (ψ(y)) ≤ C for all y, and every η′ ∈ D^{k+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) compatible near cyl(spt X) with (G, ψ), where G(y) := F₀(tl(y)) + t(y)·(F₁(tl(y)) − F₀(tl(y))), one has |Z(η′)| ≤ c·s·L^k·B·C. Let (SH) denote the conjunction of (E0), (E1) and (Aff) above (verbatim the frozen statement of the sibling smooth_homotopy, Lean name dph_smooth_homotopy), and let (Prod) denote the proposition: for all m, k ∈ ℕ and every X ∈ D_k(ℝ^m) with M(X) < ∞ there is Z ∈ D_{k+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) with ProdChar(X, Z) (this is the existence assertion of part (I) of the frozen statement of the sibling interval_product, dph_interval_product, with its other assertions dropped). C^∞ means ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞), spt = support, and a map g is proper on F if g⁻¹(K) ∩ F is compact for every compact K. Claim: assume (Prod) and (SH). Then for all m, m′, k ∈ ℕ, every X ∈ D_k(ℝ^m) with M(X) < ∞ such that M(∂Y) < ∞ for every j ∈ ℕ and Y ∈ D_{j+1}(ℝ^m) with k = j + 1 and HEq Y X, every G : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′} proper on spt X, all sequences (G_n), (G′_n) of C^∞ maps ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′}, all open O, O′ ⊆ ℝ^m with spt X ⊆ O and spt X ⊆ O′, and all L, L′ ∈ ℝ such that eventually ‖fderiv ℝ G_n x‖ ≤ L for all x ∈ O, eventually ‖fderiv ℝ G′_n x‖ ≤ L′ for all x ∈ O′, G_n → G uniformly on O and G′_n → G uniformly on O′, and for every ω ∈ D^k(ℝ^{m′}) and all sequences (η_n), (η′_n) in D^k(ℝ^m) such that eventually η_n is compatible with (G_n, ω) near spt X and eventually η′_n is compatible with (G′_n, ω) near spt X: X(η′_n) − X(η_n) → 0 as n → ∞.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Step 1 (comparison lemma) of the supplied proof of lipschitz_pushforward, with the constants and the ε-argument made explicit. Notation: for maps F₀, F₁ : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′}, H[F₀, F₁](y) := F₀(tl(y)) + t(y)·(F₁(tl(y)) − F₀(tl(y))) is the affine homotopy appearing in (Aff); for a test form ψ, dψ := exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ _ ψ, whose underlying form is exteriorDerivative ψ; |·| = covectorEuclideanNorm. Assume (Prod) and (SH) and fix m, m′, k, X, G, (G_n), (G′_n), O, O′, L, L′, ω, (η_n), (η′_n) as in the claim.

0. (Preliminaries.)
(i) spt X = univ ∖ zeroRegion(X) is closed, the zero region being open. If k = j + 1, the HEq hypothesis applied to j and Y := X (k = j + 1, HEq X X) gives M(∂X) < ∞; moreover spt ∂X ⊆ spt X by part (1) of the reused support_lemmas (with U := univ), and spt ∂X is closed.
(ii) (Bounded test forms.) For every test form ψ on ℝ^{m′} the function y ↦ |ψ(y)| is continuous (|·| is the square root of a finite sum of squares of the evaluations α ↦ α(e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(q)}), each continuous linear in α, and ψ is continuous) and vanishes outside the compact set tsupport ψ; hence it is bounded, and there is C_ψ ≥ 0 with |ψ(y)| ≤ C_ψ for all y. Put C₁ := C_{dω} and, if k = j + 1, C₂ := C_ω.
(iii) (Products.) By (Prod) for X there is Z ∈ D_{k+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) with ProdChar(X, Z). If k = j + 1, then ∂X ∈ D_j(ℝ^m) has M(∂X) < ∞, and (Prod) for ∂X gives Z′ ∈ D_{j+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) with ProdChar(∂X, Z′).
(iv) (Constants.) (Aff) for (m, m′, k) gives c ≥ 0; if k = j + 1, (Aff) for (m, m′, j) gives c′ ≥ 0. Put O″ := O ∩ O′ (open, spt X ⊆ O″), L″ := max(max(L, L′), 0) ≥ 0 and B := M(X).toReal ≥ 0, so that M(X) = ENNReal.ofReal B because M(X) < ∞; if k = j + 1 put B′ := M(∂X).toReal ≥ 0, so M(∂X) = ENNReal.ofReal B′. Let C₀ := c·B·C₁ if k = 0 and C₀ := c·L″^{j+1}·B·C₁ + c′·L″^j·B′·C₂ if k = j + 1; then C₀ ≥ 0.
(v) (The affine homotopy.) If F₀, F₁ are C^∞, then H := H[F₀, F₁] is C^∞, because t and tl are continuous linear maps and sums, products with the C^∞ scalar function t, and compositions of C^∞ maps are C^∞. Since t(cons(s, x)) = s and tl(cons(s, x)) = x, we have H(cons(0, x)) = F₀(x) + 0 = F₀(x) and H(cons(1, x)) = F₀(x) + (F₁(x) − F₀(x)) = F₁(x) for all x; i.e. the maps x ↦ H(cons(0, x)) and x ↦ H(cons(1, x)) are F₀ and F₁ (so they also have the same derivatives).
1. (Core estimate.) Claim: let F₀, F₁ : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′} be C^∞ and s ≥ 0, and assume: dist(F₁(x), F₀(x)) ≤ s, ‖fderiv ℝ F₀ x‖ ≤ L″ and ‖fderiv ℝ F₁ x‖ ≤ L″ for all x ∈ O″; F₀ is proper on spt X; H := H[F₀, F₁] is proper on cyl(spt X); and η₀, η₁ ∈ D^k(ℝ^m) are compatible near spt X with (F₀, ω) and (F₁, ω), respectively. Then |X(η₁) − X(η₀)| ≤ C₀·s.
Proof of the claim. By 0(v), η₀ and η₁ are compatible near spt X with (x ↦ H(cons(0, x)), ω) and (x ↦ H(cons(1, x)), ω), which is the form required in (E0) and (E1). H is C^∞ and proper on cyl(spt X), so the reused compatible_form (with P := m + 1, Q := m′, U := V := univ, A := cyl(spt X), f := H) applied to the test form dω gives η′ ∈ D^{k+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) compatible with (H, dω) near cyl(spt X), where the underlying form of dω is exteriorDerivative ω.
Case k = 0. (E0), applied to X, Z, G := H, ω, η₀, η₁ and η′, gives X(η₁) − X(η₀) = Z(η′). (Aff) for (m, m′, 0), applied to X, Z, F₀, F₁, O″, s, L″, B, ψ := dω, C := C₁ and η′ (its hypotheses are exactly: 0 ≤ s, 0 ≤ L″, 0 ≤ B, M(X) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal B, ProdChar(X, Z), F₀ and F₁ C^∞, O″ open with spt X ⊆ O″, the distance and derivative bounds on O″, F₀ proper on spt X, |dω(y)| ≤ C₁ for all y, and η′ compatible near cyl(spt X) with (H[F₀, F₁], dω)), gives |Z(η′)| ≤ c·s·L″^0·B·C₁ = C₀·s.
Case k = j + 1. The reused compatible_form applied to ω gives also θ′ ∈ D^{j+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) and an open N′ ⊇ cyl(spt X) on which θ′ is compatible with (H, ω). (E1), applied to X, Z, Z′, G := H, ω, η₀, η₁, η′ and θ′, gives X(η₁) − X(η₀) = Z(η′) + Z′(θ′). (Aff) for (m, m′, j + 1), applied to X, Z, ψ := dω, C := C₁ and η′ as in the case k = 0, gives |Z(η′)| ≤ c·s·L″^{j+1}·B·C₁. (Aff) for (m, m′, j) is applied to ∂X, Z′, F₀, F₁, O″, s, L″, B′, ψ := ω, C := C₂ and θ′: its hypotheses hold because M(∂X) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal B′, ProdChar(∂X, Z′) holds, spt ∂X ⊆ spt X ⊆ O″, F₀ is proper on spt ∂X (for compact K, F₀⁻¹(K) ∩ spt ∂X = (F₀⁻¹(K) ∩ spt X) ∩ spt ∂X is the intersection of a compact set with a closed set), and θ′ is compatible with (H, ω) near cyl(spt ∂X) on the same N′ (cyl(spt ∂X) ⊆ cyl(spt X)); it gives |Z′(θ′)| ≤ c′·s·L″^j·B′·C₂. Hence |X(η₁) − X(η₀)| ≤ |Z(η′)| + |Z′(θ′)| ≤ C₀·s. This proves the claim.
2. (Eventual hypotheses.) Fix ε > 0. Each of the following finitely many statements holds for all sufficiently large n, hence all of them hold simultaneously for all n ≥ some n_ε: (a) ‖fderiv ℝ G_n x‖ ≤ L for all x ∈ O and ‖fderiv ℝ G′_n x‖ ≤ L′ for all x ∈ O′ (hypotheses); (b) dist(G(x), G_n(x)) < ε for all x ∈ O and dist(G(x), G′_n(x)) < ε for all x ∈ O′ (uniform convergence, Metric.tendstoUniformlyOn_iff); (c) η_n is compatible with (G_n, ω) near spt X and η′_n is compatible with (G′_n, ω) near spt X (hypotheses).
3. (Applying the core estimate.) Let n ≥ n_ε, F₀ := G_n and F₁ := G′_n; both are C^∞, hence continuous. On O″ we have ‖fderiv ℝ F₀ x‖ ≤ L ≤ L″, ‖fderiv ℝ F₁ x‖ ≤ L′ ≤ L″ and dist(F₁(x), F₀(x)) ≤ dist(F₁(x), G(x)) + dist(G(x), F₀(x)) < 2ε. On spt X ⊆ O″ we have dist(F₀(x), G(x)) ≤ ε and dist(F₁(x), G(x)) ≤ ε; since spt X is closed and G is proper on spt X, part (a) of proper_transfer (g := F₀, d := ε) shows that F₀ is proper on spt X, and part (b) of proper_transfer (d := ε) shows that H[F₀, F₁] is proper on cyl(spt X). The core estimate (step 1) with s := 2ε, η₀ := η_n and η₁ := η′_n gives |X(η′_n) − X(η_n)| ≤ 2C₀·ε.
4. (Conclusion.) Let δ > 0 and ε := δ/(2C₀ + 1) > 0. By steps 2 and 3, for all sufficiently large n, |X(η′_n) − X(η_n) − 0| ≤ 2C₀·ε = δ·2C₀/(2C₀ + 1) < δ. Hence X(η′_n) − X(η_n) → 0. ∎

Formalization remark (not part of the mathematical argument): when (E0)/(E1) and (Aff) are instantiated, take G := the explicit lambda y ↦ F₀(tl y) + t(y)·(F₁(tl y) − F₀(tl y)) exactly as written in (Aff); the endpoint identities of 0(v) are then the function equalities (x ↦ H(cons(0, x))) = F₀ and (x ↦ H(cons(1, x))) = F₁, proved by funext from t(cons(s, x)) = s and tl(cons(s, x)) = x (both hold by rfl), and the compatibility hypotheses of (E0)/(E1) follow by rewriting with them.
proof_key_steps: Preliminaries: spt X closed; M(∂X) < ∞ from the HEq hypothesis with Y := X; spt ∂X ⊆ spt X (support_lemmas); sup bounds C₁ for dω and C₂ for ω; products Z of X and Z′ of ∂X from (Prod); constants c, c′ from (Aff).
The affine homotopy H[F₀, F₁] is C^∞ with H(cons(0,·)) = F₀ and H(cons(1,·)) = F₁, so η₀, η₁ are compatible in the form required by (E0)/(E1).
Core estimate: compatible_form gives η′ (for dω) and θ′ (for ω) near cyl(spt X); (E0)/(E1) and (Aff) for X and ∂X give |X(η₁) − X(η₀)| ≤ C₀·s.

Eventually: derivative bounds, dist(G_n, G), dist(G′_n, G) < ε on O, O′, compatibility; then dist(G′_n, G_n) < 2ε on O ∩ O′ and proper_transfer gives properness of G_n on spt X and of the homotopy on cyl(spt X).
Hence eventually |X(η′_n) − X(η_n)| ≤ 2C₀ε; with ε := δ/(2C₀ + 1) the difference tends to 0.

audit.reason: The explicit Prod and SH assumptions are correctly directed upstream inputs. The proof treats zero and successor degrees, specializes HEq correctly, supplies properness and compatible forms, and obtains a nonnegative constant independent of epsilon. Its final epsilon argument proves precisely the stated convergence.
